{{Youmay|a Mandalorian diamond|[[Ka'rta Tor]], a Mandalorian war chant}}
[[File:JangoSansHelmet-SWE.png|thumb|Jango Fett's armor featured the Iron Heart]]
{{Quote|At the juncture of the breastplates sits a small lozenge-shaped piece of armor known as ''ka'rta beskar'' or tapul.|Tor Vizsla, ''Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad''|<ref name="TBHC">''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]''</ref>}}
The '''Iron Heart''',<ref name="Blog" /> also known as '''''ka'rta beskar''''' in the Mandalorian [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']],<ref name="TBHC" /> and colloquially as the '''Mandalorian Diamond''', was an ancient symbol used by the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] people since the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] and [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]] in [[3653 BBY]].<ref name="Star Wars: The Old Republic">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]''</ref> It was notably featured on the [[Breast/Legends|chest]] part of the [[Mandalorian armor/Legends|Mandalorian Shock Trooper Armor]]. Its usage was widespread amongst the members of [[Ung Kusp|Ung Kusp's]] [[Unidentified Mandalorian clan (Ung Kusp)|clan]] prior to the Mandalorian's involvement in the [[New Sith Wars]].<ref name="Prototypes">{{StoryCite|story=Prototypes|book=Star Wars: Visionaries}}</ref> When [[Mandalore the Uniter]] standardized and mass produced Mandalorian armor after [[1051 BBY]], the Iron Heart became a core component of Mandalorian armor design.<ref name="TBHC" /> During the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], the Iron Heart was used in one way or another by both the traditional Mandalorian warriors, as well as the pacifist [[New Mandalorians/Legends|New Mandalorians]]. The Iron Heart saw use in various architectural works throughout New Mandalorian society, on police equipment, and even featured on civilian attire.<ref name="Blog">{{SW|url=news/mandalorian-mysteries-the-icons-of-mandalore|text=Mandalorian Mysteries: The Icons of Mandalore|int=Mandalorian Mysteries: The Icons of Mandalore|nolive=1}}</ref>

The symbol was noted in ''[[Ba'jurne Kyr'tsad Mando'ad]]'', a manifesto of the [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] Mandalorian splinter group. The document was supposedly [[Author/Legends|written]] by the movement's [[Secret Mandalore|leader]], [[Tor Vizsla]]&mdash;although the Death Watch's opponent [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]] doubted its authenticity&mdash;and was eventually included in the [[Book/Legends|book]] ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code]]'' by Jango's son, the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]].<ref name="TBHC" />

==Behind the scenes==
In ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'', the canonical Mando'a name of the Iron Heart was given as ''ka'rta beskar''. However, the proper spelling of the first word is ''kar'ta'' and the rules of that language established by [[Karen Traviss]] state the adjectives come before the noun they modify&mdash;as seen in ''cin vhetin'', in which ''cin'' is "white."<ref name="Mando'a dico">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref> Furthermore, the word ''beskar'' is a noun, and would require the addition of a suffix, either ''-la'' or ''-yc'', to be used as an adjective.<ref name="Mando'a gram">{{WebCite|url=http://karentraviss.com/page20/page26/page25/index.html|text=Mando'a grammar|archivedate=20111125225244}}</ref> According to those rules, the most proper Mando'a form to convey the meaning of "Iron Heart" would be ''Beskaryc Kar'ta''.<ref name="Mando'a dico" /><ref name="Mando'a gram" />
